declarations.docstring: The family of one-vertex types used to carry a prescribed finite number of loops.
The canonical vertex in the type associated with a given loop count.
A path-indexed basis for every module hom space identifies the module hom-dimension matrix with the path-counting matrix.
For a finite quiver without nontrivial closed paths, the matrix attached to its distinguished module family is the path-counting matrix.
A vertex occurring along a path determines a factorization of that path as a composite.
A finite quiver with finite arrow sets and no nontrivial closed paths has finitely many paths between any two vertices.
In a quiver with finite vertices and arrows, the paths of fixed endpoints and fixed length form a finite type.
The algebra homomorphism from a finitely generated free algebra to its scalar field that sends every generator to zero.
The free-algebra augmentation vanishes on each canonical generator.
The algebra equivalence between the free algebra on finitely many generators and the path algebra of the corresponding loop quiver.
The algebra homomorphism from a finite free algebra to the path algebra of the corresponding loop quiver.
Mapping from a loop-quiver path algebra to the free algebra and back is the identity.
The round trip from the loop-quiver path algebra through the free algebra fixes every arrow element.
The round trip from the loop-quiver path algebra through the free algebra fixes every path element.
The map from the free algebra to the loop-quiver path algebra sends a generator to its indexed loop arrow.
The path algebra of a finite quiver satisfies the indexed algebra property at index one.
The algebra invariant of a free algebra on at least one generator is one.
The algebra invariant of a finite-quiver path algebra is one whenever the quiver has an arrow.
Each vertex type in the finite loop-quiver family is finite.
Each vertex type in the finite loop-quiver family has exactly one element.
The loop arrow selected by an index at the canonical vertex of a loop quiver.
The quiver structure with the prescribed finite family of loops on its unique vertex.
A free algebra with at least one generator does not satisfy the indexed algebra property at index zero.
The natural-number matrix recording the path counts between pairs of vertices of a quiver.
The ordered list of vertices visited by a quiver path, including both endpoints.
The list of vertices visited by a path has length one more than the number of arrows in the path.
When all closed paths are trivial, the vertices visited by any path have no repetitions.
The algebra homomorphism from a loop-quiver path algebra to the free algebra on its loop indices.
The map from a loop-quiver path algebra to the free algebra sends an arrow to the generator indexed by that arrow.
Mapping from the free algebra to the loop-quiver path algebra and back is the identity.
There is a unique algebra homomorphism from the loop-quiver path algebra that sends vertices to one and arrows to their indexed free generators.
The map from a loop-quiver path algebra to the free algebra sends every vertex element to one.
In a finite quiver without nontrivial closed paths, every path has length strictly less than the number of vertices.
The path-algebra element associated with the unique vertex of a loop quiver is the multiplicative identity.
